newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Saab expects Swedish sales to hit 20,000 '97.
newsitem.headline: Saab expects Swedish sales to hit 20,000 '97.

text.p: Saab Opel Sweden on Thursday estimated its sales would reach close to 20,000 new Saabs in Sweden in 1997 compared to 15,617 in 1996.
"The uncertainty over company cars has been lifted. Now companies are putting in orders," company spokesman Torsten Aman told Reuters, referring to new company car legislation.
"We think that the total Swedish market will increase to about 200,000 cars this year and we estimate to have about 10 percent of that market."
The reason for the positive forecasts is the increased interest from customers.
"The order books promise a strong first quarter of 1997 for sales in Sweden," Aman said.
Last year ended with a strong lift in sales for Saab in December when Saab registrations jumped 21 percent compared to an overall market rise of 14 percent, Saab said in a statement.
The situation is also looking good for early 1997.
"We have cause to count on a good start of 1997 - not least as later in the year we will add our third model series," Bjarne Egstrand, managing director for Saab Opel Sweden, said in a statement.
In December sales of the Saab 900 increased by 63 percent to 1,033 cars while sales of the Saab 9000 fell by seven percent to 860 cars.
In calendar year 1996 Saab's Swedish sales fell overall by 15 percent. The Saab 900 slipped by 11 percent to 7,909 cars while sales of the Saab 9000 declined 19 percent to 7,708 bilar.
